hook.text: Before a model can predict the future, it needs to know the present—data assimilation provides that starting point.

buildup.text: Millions of observations from stations, satellites, balloons, and aircraft are blended into the model's grid.

discovery.text: The model's previous forecast is combined with new observations—weighting each based on reliability and coverage.

twist.text: A single bad observation can corrupt the analysis—quality control rejects thousands of suspect readings every cycle.

climax.text: Data assimilation uses more computing power than running the forecast itself—it's the hardest part of NWP.

punchline.text: Garbage in, garbage out—so assimilation is everything.

quiz.question: What is data assimilation in weather forecasting?
options: Blending observations into the model's initial state
